claims.text: Rapid thin-film deposition reduces grain size and increases the surface-to-volume ratio of non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys.
Reduced grain size and increased surface-to-volume ratio increase continuous nanoscale crystal-ordering fluctuations.
Distributed crystal-ordering fluctuations weaken the energy barrier for the magnetostructural transition.
Weaker transition barriers broaden the magnetocaloric response.
Weaker transition barriers substantially reduce hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Conventional arc-melted or melt-spun FeMnNiGeSi material has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
Conventional FeMnNiGeSi material exhibits a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with high hysteresis.
Sputter deposition or another rapid-solidification coating process will induce a nanocrystalline FeMnNiGeSi microstructure.
Nanocrystalline grain boundaries enable spatially heterogeneous crystal-ordering fluctuations.
Nanoscale heterogeneity causes local regions to transform at different temperatures rather than through a uniform sharp transition.
A distribution of local transformation temperatures produces a broader and smoother entropy-change profile.
A distributed transition reduces hysteretic energy loss.
The thin-film or nanostructured alloy will have a broader, lower-amplitude magnetocaloric entropy-change peak than the bulk baseline.
The thin-film or nanostructured alloy will have a significantly smaller magnetic hysteresis-loop area than the bulk baseline.
Increasing surface-to-volume ratio through thin-film processing will improve heat-exchange rates.
The predicted behavior should apply particularly to submicron-thickness FeMnNiGeSi samples where surface-to-volume effects prevail.
Excessive annealing or overcooling may produce phase separation and place samples outside the proposed regime.
The hysteresis reduction and entropy-profile shift depend sensitively on nanograin-size distribution and interfacial quality.
